## ▶ PHASE A (2026-09-13): the D-27 meal rebuild, T-195 to T-199

**Source for all five:** `docs/work/NEXT-SESSION.md` "Phase A", `docs/work/DECISIONS.md` D-27 with answers 1–9 (hold lifted 2026-09-13), and the map `docs/work/intake/D-27-rebuild-map.md`. Everything in them is decided by Rajeev and is not reopened.

**State at reservation:** `HEAD` `940de0a`, tree clean except the main session's progress line in `NEXT-SESSION.md`. Highest migration on disk `V134`, so the next free is **`V135`**. Highest 4xx error code `KMS-400151`.

**Waves.** Four, because each later task reads what the earlier one built:
- **D27-1:** T-195 alone (schema, purge, reseed). Every other task needs its tables.
- **D27-2:** T-196 and T-197 together. Disjoint paths; they meet only at the seams below, which are fixed here so neither builder invents the other side.
- **D27-3:** T-198 alone. It owns `frontend/lib/api.ts` and reads the finished backend.
- **D27-4:** T-199 alone, after T-198, because both need `api.ts` and the shift form.
After D27-2 and D27-4 the work manager runs the merged-tree check, including every repo-wide guard in `docs/work/README.md` lesson 3a. **Release rule (brief):** before deploying the purge, the release agent takes an on-demand backup of the staging Cloud SQL database and records its id here. No backup, no deploy. Production must still hold no temple data when this ships, or the purge must not ship as written.

**Reservations, made by the work manager in one pass:**
- **Migrations:** `V135`, `V136`, `V137` for T-195 (purge, schema, reseed), and `V138` spare for T-195 only. `V139` for T-196 and `V140` for T-197, each only if it finds it needs one; an unused number stays unused.
- **`error/ErrorCode.java`**, written by the work manager, for T-197:
  - `MEAL_ALREADY_HAS_SHIFT` **KMS-400152** (409): *"This meal already has a volunteer shift."* / *"Open the meal in the planner and change the shift it already has."* Thrown when the partial unique index refuses a second live shift for one meal (two saves at once).
  - `MEAL_SHIFT_KEEPS_ITS_MEAL` **KMS-400153** (409): *"A shift for a meal keeps that meal's date and meal."* / *"If it is no longer for this meal, cancel it and ask for volunteers from the right meal in the planner."* Thrown when an update from the Volunteer shifts page changes a meal shift's date or meal.
  - `SHIFT_MEAL_LINK_INCOMPLETE` (KMS-400125) loses its thrower. It stays in the file, because codes are never reused.
- **Permissions:** none. Temple Admin, Kitchen Manager and Kitchen Staff all hold both `MANAGE_MEAL_PLANS` and `MANAGE_VOLUNTEER_SHIFTS` (`RolePermissions.java` 47/67, 109/112, 138/144), so a meal saved with its shift needs no new grant.
- **Audit enums:** `audit/AuditEntityType.java` and `audit/AuditAction.java` belong to T-196 in D27-2 (`MEAL` is added there). T-197 uses existing actions, or stops and reports.
- **`frontend/lib/api.ts`, `nav.ts`, `routes.ts`:** not stubbed. T-198 owns them outright in D27-3, and T-199 in D27-4, because each runs alone.

**Names fixed for the schema** (the work manager's call, so T-196 and T-197 can write SQL against it while T-195's proof is the only description): `meal_plan_days` (one row per temple per date), `meals` (FK to its day and to `meal_kinds.id`, `event_name`, and every per-meal field including card, recording and correction), and `meal_dishes` (the renamed `meal_plans`, so **dish ids are unchanged**, with `meal_id` FK). `meal_services` is folded into `meals` and dropped. `documents.meal_service_id` becomes `documents.meal_id`. `shifts.meal_id` is a nullable FK replacing `meal_date`, `meal_kind` and `meal_event_name`. One meal per day + kind + `lower(event_name)`, **not** partial: planning a cancelled meal again reuses its row (T-196 find-or-create), so a meal id a shift or stock movement points at is never duplicated. Easy to reverse before release.

**Reseed without stock draws** (the work manager's call): the two recorded days are seeded as recorded figures with job card numbers, but with **no stock movements**, so on-hand is identical before and after the whole V135–V137 run, which is Answer 8's promise and the test T-195 writes. Seeding FEFO draws in SQL would also be a hand-written unit conversion, which `BaseQuantityIT` forbids.

**The seams between T-196 and T-197** (given to both builders verbatim):
1. **`shift/MealShiftDraft.java`**, written by T-197 first: `record MealShiftDraft(String title, String description, LocalTime startTime, LocalTime endTime, String location, int capacity, List<Integer> reminderOffsetsMinutes)` with `CreateShiftRequest`'s validation messages and its end-differs-from-start assertion. No date and no meal: both come from the meal.
2. **`ShiftService`** (T-197) adds `Optional<ShiftView> findForMeal(UUID mealId)`; `UUID saveForMeal(AuthenticatedUser actor, UUID mealId, MealShiftDraft draft)`, create-or-update in the caller's transaction, shift date read from the meal, messages and reminder scheduling after commit only; and `int cancelForMeal(UUID mealId, String reason)`, in the caller's transaction, the existing cancellation message after commit, returning how many were told. `list(from, to, includeCancelled)`, `roster(id)` and `listCountingTowardMeals(from, to)` keep their parameters. `ShiftView` replaces `mealDate, mealKind, mealEventName` with `UUID mealId, String mealKind, String mealEventName`, the last two read through the FK for labels.
3. **`ServedMeal`** (T-196): `serviceId` becomes `UUID mealId`; `ServedMealService.list(LocalDate, LocalDate)` keeps its parameters.
4. **`MealCrewService`** (T-197): `crewFor(from, to)`, `crewIfAway(staffProfileId, from, to)` and `suggestedCrew(mealKind)` keep their parameters; `MealCrewView` gains `UUID mealId`.
5. **`MealMoment`** (T-197): `record MealMoment(UUID mealId, LocalDate date, LocalTime readyBy, String mealKind, String eventName)` with `isFor(UUID mealId)`. `WorkforceService.countFor` keeps its parameters. `MealKindService`'s rename cascade is removed by T-196, so it stops using `MealMoment` and `ShiftService` for it.

### T-195 — A meal is a row: schema, the per-temple purge with stock kept level, and the minimum reseed
- **id:** T-195 · **wave:** D27-1 · **state:** **proven** 2026-09-14, released 2026-09-14 (see Phase A release below) · **proof:** `docs/work/proof/T-195.md`

The nine must-be-green classes pass (79 tests); the negative control failed 2 of 10 on on-hand and adjustments. `CateringMigrationIT` and `DeliveryPinBackfillIT` are pinned to V134. The full suite is 2648 tests with 1111 failed, and most of that is one cascade: a meal-reading class's cleanup dies and leaves the `radha-govinda` temple, so about 90 unrelated classes fail on its slug. **Worth knowing for D27-2:** every PDF (recipe, purchase order, work order, donation receipt) is broken until `DocumentGenerationService` reads `documents.meal_id`, and `StaffScheduleIT` fails through `WorkforceService`. The proof's "D27-2 worklist" is the list. "The temple's own recipes" was read as any ACTIVE row in the temple's `recipes`, library copies included.
- **source:** NEXT-SESSION.md Phase A task 1; D-27 answers 2, 8, 9.
- **what:** V135 purges, per temple with `app.tenant_id` set, everything Answer 9 deletes, first inserting one `ADJUSTMENT` movement per ingredient (and per batch, if movements carry one) equal to the on-hand net of the meal movements it deletes, and resets the job card counter. V136 builds the schema named above, with `enable_tenant_rls()` on every new table, the partial unique index for one live shift per meal, and every function, trigger, check and view that names the old columns redefined. V137 reseeds per Answer 9, per temple, only where the temple has its own recipes. A new `MealRebuildMigrationIT` proves on-hand is identical before and after, that the purge deleted rows under RLS, that the uniqueness rules refuse, and that the reseed produced what Answer 9 lists.
- **paths:** `backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V135__*.sql`, `V136__*.sql`, `V137__*.sql`, (`V138__*.sql` only if needed); `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/meal/MealRebuildMigrationIT.java` (new); `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/TenantLoopMigrationIT.java`; `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/meal/CateringMigrationIT.java`; `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/meal/DeliveryPinBackfillIT.java`; and only if forced: `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/inventory/BaseQuantityIT.java`, `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/tenancy/RowLevelSecurityIT.java`, `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/tenant/TenantDeletionIT.java`, `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/tenant/TenantExportIT.java`, `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/inventory/StockMovementLedgerIT.java`.

Worse, T-197's server sends "The times changed to …" on every shift, so a plain shift moved to another date *and* new times would tell volunteers only about the times. **The rule now being built:** the times message goes only when the date is unchanged. Ownership checked: no other builder is in the tree; T-197 holds `shift/**` backend, T-199 holds `app/volunteers/**`, disjoint. The work manager's call that a plain shift's **time-only** change also sends the message (T-197 built it for every shift): reversible, and flagged for Rajeev.

### T-200 — The purchase order PDF goes with the vendor's WhatsApp message (item 1, carries T-182)
- **id:** T-200 · **wave:** PB-2 · **state:** **proven** 2026-09-14, after one return · **proof:** `docs/work/proof/T-200.md`
- **rework result:**
  - Option 1 was built. When Send on WhatsApp finds no READY sheet, it renders one on the spot, in the vendor's language, before the message is queued.
  - If the render fails, the press is refused with 409 `KMS-400155`, the transaction rolls back, and nothing is queued. The test runs on a sent order, because test data cannot make a draft's render fail; the draft rollback rests on the transaction.
  - The adapter still refuses any sheet that is not READY.
  - Negative control: without the render, 7 tests went red; restored and checked with `cmp`.
  - Full backend 2,721 tests, 0 failed. Full frontend 1,900; tsc clean with `appId` required, lint and build clean.
  - A press with no READY sheet now waits for one render.
- **first result:**
  - Full backend 2,714 tests, 0 failed. Full frontend 1,900 tests; tsc, lint and build clean.
  - Negative control: 2 send tests went red; restored and checked with `cmp`.
  - V141 `whatsapp_app_id`. V142 rewrites stored "Press Reload" reasons per tenant.
  - A temple with no App ID gets a stored reason naming the box, and no upload.
  - A translated order sends the translated sheet.
- **sent back because:**
  - Pressing Send on WhatsApp on a draft queues its sheet, and the notification job can run first. The adapter then refuses the channel, the cascade falls to SMS or email, and the send usually ends FAILED with nothing shown to the person who pressed it.
  - That meets "never send without it" but not the brief's "generate one or refuse clearly".
  - Work manager's call: generate the sheet synchronously. If that is not workable, or the render fails, refuse at press time with **`KMS-400155` `PO_SHEET_NOT_READY`**, now written into `ErrorCode.java`.
  - Contract widened to `document/DocumentGenerationService.java` and `document/PurchaseOrderDocumentController.java`. `orders/[id]/page.tsx` and `order-detail.test.tsx` are granted only if the screen must change. Grepped: no live builder holds them.
- **still for the main session on staging:**
  - Whether `/<APP_ID>/uploads` accepts the stored System User token. If it does not, the stored reason wrongly blames the App ID.
  - The send's document field names (`id`, `filename`).
  - After deploy, every connected temple's templates button reads "1 template changed". Registering a header at Meta is hard to reverse once approved.
- **source:** NEXT-SESSION.md Phase B item 1 ("MUST"), and the T-182 row below, which holds the Meta docs findings and the app id analysis.
- **what:**
  - Add a Meta **App ID** box to Settings → WhatsApp.
    - It uses the same read-only / Edit / Save pattern as the other boxes, and is shown in full because it is not a secret.
    - It is stored in `tenant_settings` (V141).
  - Register the purchase order template with a `DOCUMENT` header.
    - The brief calls it `purchase_order`. In code it is `NotificationTemplate.PO_DELIVERY` / `po_delivery`.
    - The header's example is a handle from Meta's resumable upload: `POST /<APP_ID>/uploads`, then the handle.
    - The body wording stays as approved.
  - At send, `PurchaseOrderDeliveryService.sendViaWhatsApp` already puts the latest READY sheet's `documentId` in the params. Upload that PDF to `/<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/media` (or send a link) and send it as the header document.
  - Send the PDF as it is: the translated sheet if the order was translated, otherwise the English original. `latestReadySheet` currently ignores language, so check how translated sheets are stored.
  - If there is no READY sheet, generate one or refuse clearly. Never send without it.
  - Make the template comparison (`WhatsAppTemplateComparison`) and the template fingerprint aware of the header.
  - A temple with no App ID gets a stored refusal reason that names the App ID box.
  - The "Press Reload" fold-in is already done in code by T-188 (`TEMPLATES_BUTTON`). What is left: stored entries in `tenant_settings.whatsapp_refused_templates` may still carry the three old sentences (from `git log -S"Press Reload"`):
    - "…Press Reload to try again."
    - "…Press Reload again once the review is over."
    - "…Press Reload again tomorrow."
  - Rewrite those to the T-188 wording in V142, looping per tenant with `app.tenant_id` set. If the proof shows no stored row can hold them, leave V142 unwritten.
  - **Builders never call Meta, press Reload or send.** Every Meta call is proven against a stub HTTP server. No token is read or handled.
  - Nobody knows yet whether the temple's system-user token is accepted by `/uploads`. The main session verifies it on staging after release, with Rajeev if a credential is needed.
- **paths:**

    - `MetaWhatsAppClient.java`
    - `WhatsAppChannelAdapter.java`

    - `backend/src/main/java/org/iskcon/kms/purchaseorder/PurchaseOrderDeliveryService.java`

## ▶ T-168 (2026-09-13) — Meta's "already exists" answers are stored as refusals; backend only, beside T-160

### T-168 — A template Meta already holds is recorded as refused

- **source:** staging, 2026-09-13, reported by the main session after T-159's deploy. Save on Settings → WhatsApp at 01:35:58Z (request `b5432e55…`) took 60.07s and returned 200. The log read *"Submitted 7 of 20 WhatsApp templates"*: the six reworded templates and `whatsapp_connection_check`. The other 13 were stored as refused:
  - **11**, Meta: *"There is already English content for this template. You can create a new template and try again."* They are `leave_revoked`, `leave_declined`, `leave_approved`, `staff_schedule_updated`, `shift_cancelled`, `removed_from_shift`, `waitlist_promoted`, `shift_signup_confirmed`, `volunteer_shift_reminder`, `donation_receipt` and `wishlist_sponsorship_converted`.
  - **2**, Meta: *"The category UTILITY doesn't match the one that's already associated with this template, MARKETING."* They are `donation_thank_you` and `wishlist_gift_split`; Meta re-categorised both itself.
- **The defect:** `MetaWhatsAppClient.createTemplate` recognises an existing template only when Meta's English text contains "already exists". Meta's real answer for an existing template does not, so it comes back REFUSED. All 13 are on staging in `refusedTemplates`, with the generic reason *"Meta did not accept this message. Press Save to try again…"*. That is a false alarm with wrong advice, since pressing Save again gets the same answer. Once the Settings redesign shows the list, every temple that saves twice would see 13 false refusals.
- **Confirmed known limit, recorded:** a second Save does not send existing templates back to Meta's approval queue. Existing wording is never updated (T-159's known limit).
- **wave:** runs beside T-160, whose paths are frontend only; checked disjoint.
- **state:** **released** 2026-09-13, one release and one staging deploy with T-160; proven the same day. **Already exists is now classified by code:** Meta documents code `100`, subcode **`2388024`** ("Content in This Language Already Exists") on its template-management page, read from the raw page. The English sentence stays as a fallback marked STOPGAP. **The category mismatch has no documented code** (not on the error-codes, template-management or categorization pages), so it uses a marked text fallback, checked first in case the same answer also carries `2388024`. A new outcome `HELD_UNDER_ANOTHER_CATEGORY` is stored with `kind` and the reason *"Meta holds this message as marketing, which some countries do not deliver."* (true per Meta's per-user-limits page). An already-held template is not stored at all. Entries without a `kind` read back as `REFUSED`. **Date decision:** a template held under another category counts toward "templates submitted", since Meta holds it. **Replace on save confirmed** and now pinned with a non-empty after-state: staging's 13 false entries read back, then a staging-shaped save leaves exactly the two marketing entries. A DEBUG line logs Meta's raw `error.code`, `error_subcode` and `error_user_title` on every non-2xx answer. `api.ts` untouched; the GET now carries `kind`. Builder's run 2: 810/810 (`MetaTemplateOutcomeTest` 11, `WhatsAppTemplateSubmissionIT` 12, `WhatsAppTestSendIT` 8, `WhatsAppLastSentIT` 6, `MetaTemplateRulesTest` 6, `ErrorCodeTest` 767). Its run 1 was red from a test seed that broke V55's shape check, fixed in the test only. Control (T-159's English check restored): 8 of 23 red, reproducing staging's 13 false refusals exactly; restore by `cmp`. **Needs the main session:** root logging is INFO, so the DEBUG line will not show on staging unless the revision sets `LOGGING_LEVEL_ORG_ISKCON_KMS_NOTIFICATION_METAWHATSAPPCLIENT=DEBUG`. **Follow-ups:** after one staging Save with DEBUG on, confirm subcode `2388024` on the 11 and note any subcode on the two marketing ones, then retire the fallbacks; `plainReason` could use the documented `2388293` and `2388299` instead of English; the screen should show `HELD_UNDER_ANOTHER_CATEGORY` differently from a refusal (T-169). **Merged backend check, work manager, no builder in the tree:** run 1, the six contract classes, `--rerun-tasks`, **810/810**; run 2, the tests outside the contract that use the WhatsApp client, settings or templates (`CommunicationIT` 14, `NotificationIT` 7, `NotificationSendE2EIT` 1, `NotificationTemplateTest` 5, `WhatsAppChannelAdapterTest` 4, `PurchaseOrderWhatsAppIT` 8), **39/39**. Log: `scratchpad/merged-backend-T168.log`. **Released with T-160 as `5b4cbed`; staging `kms-staging-api-00157-4pt`.** **Verified on staging 2026-09-13 by the main session as the Temple Admin:** Save on Settings → WhatsApp at 02:27:30Z (request `846079e9…`) logged at 02:28:04Z *"Submitted 20 of 20 WhatsApp templates for temple f935450b…: 0 new, 18 already held, 2 held under another category"*. It took about 34 seconds against 60 before, because nothing new went to review. **The 13 false refusals are gone and the two marketing templates are classified correctly.** The screen shows *"Last checked 13 Sept 2026, 07:57"*. The `refusedTemplates` body was not re-read through the API; the log breakdown is the evidence. The DEBUG line with Meta's raw subcodes was not captured. **Confirmed limit:** Save cannot move `donation_thank_you` or `wishlist_gift_split` back to utility; that needs a category review in Meta's WhatsApp Manager, or a new name.
- **what:**
  1. Classify Meta's answer for an existing template as already existing, by Meta's error code or subcode, never by its English sentence, and do not count it as refused.
  2. Handle a category mismatch on an existing template as its own outcome, neither refused nor submitted, stored with a true plain reason, not "press Save to try again".
  3. Confirm Save replaces the stored list every time, so staging's 13 false entries clear on the next Save. T-159's proof says it already does.
  4. A test feeding each of Meta's answers through the classifier, with a negative control.
- **paths:** under `backend/src/main/java/org/iskcon/kms/notification/`: `MetaWhatsAppClient.java`, `TenantWhatsAppSettingsService.java`, `TenantWhatsAppSettings.java` (only if the stored record needs a kind) · tests under `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/notification/`: `WhatsAppTemplateSubmissionIT.java` (existing, granted), `MetaTemplateOutcomeTest.java` *(new)* · no migration expected; if one is needed, **stop and ask**, since `V129` is not reserved.

### T-160 — The shared form wrapper, proved on two forms

- **source:** Rajeev's ruling, 2026-09-11 · the main session's approval of the plan, 2026-09-13.
- **wave:** 3-0, alone.
- **state:** **released** 2026-09-13, one release and one staging deploy with T-168; proven the same day. `components/ds/Form.tsx` (a `<form noValidate>` that takes every other form attribute and forwards a ref) and `components/ds/formMessages.ts` (every sentence, in one place). On submit it reads each control's `validity` (`willValidate && !validity.valid`, no checks reimplemented), includes controls outside the tag named with `form=`, shows one red sentence per refused box, sets `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, focuses the first, and calls `onSubmit` only when everything passes. A box's sentence clears once it is put right. **Mechanism:** an empty slot placed straight after each refused box (after its wrapping `<label>`, if any), with the sentence rendered into it through a portal. A `MutationObserver` puts the slot back if React inserts a node before it, re-applies the two attributes, and drops the sentence of an unmounted box. Proved on a `Field` box and both kinds of hand-rolled box, including a re-render test. `Field.tsx` was not edited. **Sentences:** is required · must be at least / can be at most · must be on or after / on or before {date} · {HH:mm} or later / earlier · must be a whole number · can have at most 2 decimal places · must go up in steps of · must be a number / a complete date / a complete time · can be at most {n} characters · Enter an email address like name@example.com · and a catch-all *"{Name} is not valid"* that nothing reaches today (a deviation, kept so a future check is never silent). **jsdom, probed:** it blocks a click submit from a form without `novalidate` (inside and outside buttons), so control 1 is real; it never reports `badInput`, and nothing reports `tooLong` for a coded value, so those two are simulated; it skips the step check on `defaultValue`, so step tests type their values. Converted: meal kinds and occasions, 2 blank-submit tests each. `tsc` clean, 3 files 51/51, ESLint clean. Control 1 (`noValidate` removed): 15 red. Control 2 (`rangeUnderflow` branch removed): 5 red, the page saying *"Quantity is not valid"*. Restores by `cmp`. **None of the server's messages for the same rules agree in wording** (full sentences, field not named); the field-by-field list is in the proof, and aligning them is Rajeev's call. **Gaps:** no real-browser check; the box border does not turn red (needs one global `[aria-invalid="true"]` rule, outside the contract); dates print "13 Sept 2026" from the existing helper; a submit from a nested form is ignored rather than handled. **The adoption paragraph for slices A–F is in the proof, section "How a slice adopts it".** **Merged frontend check, work manager, after T-160's files were final (T-168 is backend only):** `tsc` clean, vitest **129 files / 1,565**, ESLint clean. Log: `scratchpad/merged-frontend-T160.log`. **Released with T-168 as `5b4cbed`; staging `kms-staging-api-00157-4pt` / `kms-staging-web-00145-z4p` / `kms-staging-worker-00139-jml`, schema `V128`.** **Verified in a real browser, 2026-09-13, by the main session as the Temple Admin, at `/settings/meal-kinds`, with trusted mouse and keyboard events, not scripted clicks:** the form has `noValidate=true`. A trusted click on *"Add meal kind"* with Name empty showed *"Name is required"* in red under the Name box, with no browser bubble. Focus moved to Name; `aria-invalid` became `"true"` and `aria-describedby` points at *"Name is required"*. No meal kind was added; the table stayed at 5 rows. Typing one letter cleared it: no red text left, `aria-invalid` `"false"`, nothing submitted. **The watcher that puts the sentence back after a React re-render held up in a real browser.** On that evidence the main session released 3-1.
- **what:** A form component that sets `noValidate`. On submit it reads each control's validity and accessible name, shows one plain sentence in red beside each failing box, wires `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, moves focus to the first failing field, and runs the caller's submit only when everything passes. It converts `settings/meal-kinds` and `settings/occasions` as the proving ground. Negative controls: remove `noValidate` or the wrapper and a blank-submit test goes red; remove the `min` handling and a `"0"` in a `min=1` box goes red.

T-171 must correct those tests too; no builder holds them now. **Sequencing, the work manager's recommendation:** T-171 lands **before** 3-2, so slices D to F never write tests against glued names.

(`docs/work/proof/T-171.md`). **The rule:** when `Form` reads a label for a box's name, it leaves out any element inside the label whose own classes include `text-ink-secondary`, `text-ink-muted` or `text-danger`, which are the hint, note and error colours. Only the element's own classes count, not the label's, because most labels are grey themselves. ### T-179 — My donations: a person's own successful gifts and their receipts

- **source:** Rajeev's ruling 2 above.
- **what:**
  - A signed-in volunteer sees their **COMPLETED, not voided, not anonymous** gifts: those whose `donor_account_user_id` is them, plus counter gifts whose `donor_phone` or `donor_email` matches a contact **Firebase has verified** for them.
  - "Verified" follows `TokenVerifier.VerifiedSubject`, as `PendingAccountClaim.verifiedContact` does: the token's `phone_number`, which Firebase sets only after phone sign-in, and the email only when `emailVerified`.
  - Never match by name or PAN. RLS scopes it to the temple.
  - They can download the receipt of each gift that has one issued.
  - The admin's Send receipt in `DonationDetailController` stays exactly as it is, behind `VIEW_DONATIONS`.
- **privacy tests:**
  - A gift carrying someone else's contact, or an unverified one, is never listed, and its receipt download is refused.
  - A second temple's gift is never shown.
  - A negative control removes the verified-only check and shows the leak.
- **Dependency:** T-180 changes the `donation_receipt` WhatsApp wording, *"Please ask at the temple office for a copy."*, to point at this page. It needs T-179 released first.
- **paths (checked at dispatch):** under `backend/src/main/java/org/iskcon/kms/`, `donation/` new `MyDonations*` classes, and `donation/DonationReceiptService.java` read-only unless a shared helper is unavoidable · new ITs · `frontend/app/my-donations/page.tsx` (new), `frontend/__tests__/my-donations.test.tsx` (new).
- **state:** **proven** 2026-09-13 (`docs/work/proof/T-179.md`). New `donation/MyDonation.java`, `MyDonationsService.java`, `MyDonationsController.java`, `MyDonationsIT.java`, `frontend/app/my-donations/page.tsx` and its test. `DonationReceiptService` and `DonationDetailController` untouched (`git diff --quiet`). The download reuses the public `DocumentService.receiptFor` and `openForDownload`. No migration, no error code. **Successful** = `status = 'COMPLETED'` and `voided_at IS NULL` and `is_anonymous = false`; every gift is one row in `donations` (V17 counter and goods, V38 online), with the receipt on the same row (V117) and its PDF a `DONATION_RECEIPT_PDF` document. **Verified:** phone is the token's `phone_number`; email only when `email_verified` is true. **The verified subject does not reach services today:** `AuthenticationFilter` keeps only the uid, and `AuthenticatedUser` carries the users-row contacts an administrator typed. So `MyDonationsController` verifies the same bearer token again through `TokenVerifier`, requires its uid to equal the principal's, and otherwise matches by account only. A test proves the users-row contacts match nothing. **The stranger answer:** 404 `KMS-400030`, the same as a gift id that does not exist, for someone else's gift, an unverified email, a struck, anonymous or incomplete gift, another temple's, or a gift with no receipt. A 403 would confirm the gift exists. **Privacy tests,** real endpoints as `kms_app` under RLS, `MyDonationsIT` 10/10. The second-temple test lists the other temple's gift when acting for that temple, so the absence cannot be an empty query. Targeted backend 8 classes **906/906**; frontend `tsc` and ESLint clean, `my-donations.test.tsx` 6/6. **Control 1** (match email regardless of `emailVerified`): 2 red, the unverified gift listed and its download 200 not 404; restore by `cmp`. **Control 2** (remove the query's tenant filter): **stayed green, correctly.** RLS on `donations` is the boundary, and the policy fails closed; showing a real leak needs RLS off (a migration) or `tenancy/*`, both outside the contract. Accepted as a named absence, per README. Its full vitest runs failed only in other builders' in-flight files (T-172's two, then T-169b's `settings-edit-mode.test.tsx`), which it did not edit. **Follow-ups, not queued:** (1) **counter gifts rarely match**: the counter form's donor phone has no E.164 rule, so `98765 43210` never matches a verified `+919876543210`; normalising it would need the counter form and possibly a backfill. (2) A second Firebase verification per call on these two endpoints; carrying `emailVerified` and the token's phone on `AuthenticatedUser` removes it. (3) The phone pattern is copied from `config/PhoneNumberDeserializer`, whose method is package-private. (4) A receipt whose PDF failed shows the donor 404 until an admin resends. (5) No audit entry when a donor downloads their own receipt. (6) Staff could reasonably have this page; the reservation is volunteers only. No hand test in a real browser.
- **proof:** `docs/work/proof/T-179.md`

### T-186 — A counter gift's phone is saved in +91 form, and the admin sees what was saved

- **source:** found by T-179 2026-09-13: the counter form stores the donor's phone as typed, so *"98765 43210"* never matches a verified *+919876543210* on My donations. **Decided by the main session 2026-09-13: option 2**, the coordinator's call, easy to reverse.
- **what:**
  - Normalise **new counter entries only**, and **only the unambiguous shapes**: 10 digits starting 6–9, a 0 before those, or 91 or +91 before those. Anything else is saved as typed, with no guessing.
  - The counter screen shows the saved form (*"Saved as +91 98765 43210"*) so the admin sees it before walking away.
  - **Matching in My donations stays exact**, as T-179 built it.
  - **Check `DonationLedgerService` grouping** (it groups a donor's gifts by exact phone): new +91 gifts must still group with that donor's older gifts typed without it. If they would not, say so and **do not change the ledger's matching**.
- **Negative control:** without the normaliser, a new counter gift typed *"98765 43210"* does not appear on My donations for the verified *+919876543210*; with it, it does.
- **The backfill is NOT decided here.** It is hard to reverse, and it widens who can download PAN-bearing receipts, so **it goes to Rajeev.** For that, the proof gives a read-only query counting, per temple, the existing counter rows that would change under the option 1 rule and how many would newly match a verified volunteer. The query is proven against test fixtures only, never staging; the proof says staging data is needed for the real numbers.

### T-187 — The donation ledger groups a donor's old and new phone forms together again (4c, after T-186 is released)

- **id:** T-187
- **what:** Since T-186, new counter gifts store an unambiguous Indian mobile as `+919876543210`, while older gifts keep what was typed (`98765 43210`). `DonationLedgerService` groups gifts by exact phone (`donor_phone IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ?`), so a regular donor's history splits in two. Make the ledger's grouping compare phones after the one `CounterPhone` rule is applied to **both sides at read time**, inside `DonationLedgerService`'s grouping only. Nothing stored changes. If the rule cannot run in Java for the query's shape, an SQL expression is allowed only when a test pins it to `CounterPhone` on the same shared inputs. **My donations stays exact:** `MyDonationsService` is not touched, and a test proves it does not use the normalised comparison (a counter gift stored as typed `98765 43210` still does not appear for the verified `+919876543210`). The grouped view stays under `VIEW_DONATIONS`, inside one temple. Check every caller of the ledger grouping, backend and `frontend/lib/api.ts` consumers, confirm nothing a donor or volunteer can reach reads it, and say so in the proof. Tests: an old unprefixed gift and a new `+91` gift for one donor group again; two stored strings that do not normalise to the same number stay apart; a landline kept as typed groups only with itself. Negative control: remove the read-time normalisation, and the old/new pair splits. The separator pattern copied in `PhoneNumberDeserializer`, `MyDonationsService` and `CounterPhone` is **not** part of this task, since the first two are outside its paths; it stays queued as a cleanup.
- **source:** T-186's finding that the ledger splits history; the coordinator's ruling 2026-09-13, *"Go with option 2 as T-187, after T-186 lands"*, with the conditions above.
- **paths:** `backend/src/main/java/org/iskcon/kms/donation/DonationLedgerService.java`; `backend/src/main/java/org/iskcon/kms/donation/CounterPhone.java` (only if the rule needs exposing, with no behaviour change; `CounterPhoneTest.java` with it); `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/donation/DonationLedgerIT.java`; `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/donation/MyDonationsIT.java` (exactness test only); `docs/work/proof/T-187.md`.
- **reservations:** none.
- **wave:** 4c
- **state:** **proven** 2026-09-13 (`docs/work/proof/T-187.md`). **Approach:** Java decides and SQL narrows. `donorHistory` fetches the id and stored phone of each non-anonymous gift with the same email (the email clause unchanged), keeps those whose `CounterPhone.normalise` equals the opened gift's, then loads them with the existing query. Plain Java was rejected because most counter gifts have no email, so every open would read every contactless gift. The narrowing `PHONE_NET` matches the last ten digits: looser than the rule, never stricter, and Java rejects the extras (`+44 98765 43210` tested). `phoneNetIsWiderThanTheCounterRule` pins it against PostgreSQL on `CounterPhoneTest`'s own inputs. `CounterPhone.java` and `CounterPhoneTest.java` got comments only. **Who can see it:** the only caller is `GET /api/v1/donations/ledger/donor/{donationId}` behind `VIEW_DONATIONS`, which **only the Temple Admin holds** (`RolePermissions.java` ~77–79); the work manager's note to the main session had wrongly also named Kitchen Managers. On the frontend only `app/donations/[id]/page.tsx` calls `api.donorHistory`. `DonationDetailController` never calls it, and `MyDonationsService` is unmodified and never calls `CounterPhone`. **Tests:** T-186's split assertion in `DonationLedgerIT` is replaced by grouping from every id; also covered: same email, email still exact, unequal phones apart, a landline only with itself, anonymous and contactless never join. `MyDonationsIT`: the admin's history groups the pair, and the volunteer verified as `+919876543210` sees only the `+91` gift. **Controls:** A (exact phone compare) 3 of 26 red, including the old/new pair; B (narrowing to eleven digits) the pinning test red; restore by trap, proven by `cmp`. `is_anonymous = false` can't be shown red alone, since V38 forbids contact on an anonymous gift. **Runs:** 49/49 on the donation classes, then 17 classes with the guards **969/969**. **Behaviour notes for the main session:** a landline typed two ways (`022 2345 6789`, `022-2345-6789`) still doesn't group, as before T-186. A gift whose stored phone is only spaces, with no email, now has an empty history, where before it grouped with identical spaces (unlikely: the recorder saves a blank as empty). Not driven in a browser.

### T-176 — Provisioning refuses a temple at exactly 0,0 — released

- **source:** T-174 phase 1's finding, 2026-09-13. **The main session's call, easy to reverse; it tells Rajeev.** Option 2 of three: refuse the exact pair only. One axis at 0 stays allowed, because 0 on one axis is a real place (the equator, the Greenwich meridian), as V97's comment argues for delivery pins.
- **what people see today:** Add a temple sends a blank coordinate as 0. `POST /api/v1/tenants` stores it, because `@NotNull`, the -90..90 and -180..180 ranges and V1's `NOT NULL` and `CHECK` all allow 0. The temple's calendar is worked out from 0,0. A temple stored there cannot be corrected: `PATCH` refuses any coordinate change (D-17), so it has to be deleted and added again.
- **what:** provisioning refuses latitude 0 **and** longitude 0 together (by value, so `0`, `0.0` and `0.000000` all count) with a named field error and plain words telling the Super Admin to pick the temple's place. The answer is `KMS-400002` with a `fieldErrors` entry, not a generic message. Tests: the pair is refused; 0 latitude with a real longitude passes; a real latitude with 0 longitude passes. Plus a negative control.
- **staging, checked by the main session 2026-09-13:** no temple is at 0,0. The Super Admin's list holds one temple, ISKCON South Bengaluru, whose detail (`GET /api/v1/tenants/f935450b-…`) stores latitude 12.905125, longitude 77.554514, timezone Asia/Kolkata. **No data repair is needed.** The tenant **list** view carries no coordinates; only the **detail** does.
- **reservations, made by the work manager 2026-09-13, before dispatch:** **reuse `KMS-400002 INVALID_COORDINATES`**, which existed and was **never raised anywhere** (checked by grep). Its next step was *"Latitude must be between -90 and 90, longitude between -180 and 180."*, wrong advice for a temple at 0,0, so the work manager reworded it to *"Choose the temple's place, or type its real latitude and longitude."* The message *"Those coordinates don't look right."* is unchanged. No test pinned the old text. **No new error code; `KMS-400151` is still free.** No migration (`V130` still free).

Run, not edit: `error/PhoneValidationIT.java`, `error/FieldErrorMessageTest.java`, `error/ErrorCodeTest.java`. **Not T-176's:** `ErrorCode.java` (reserved, already edited), every frontend file.

### T-174 — `Field`'s "(required)" is shown over a box that is not required — released

- **source:** found by T-166, 2026-09-13; queued by the work manager.
- **what people see today:** `components/Field.tsx` takes a `required` prop and uses it only to print *"(required)"* beside the label. It never reaches the input. On sign-in, Add a temple and Edit this temple the boxes marked *"(required)"* are not required, so a blank submit is not refused: a blank temple name or admin name goes to the server, and blank coordinates are sent as 0. Meal kinds and occasions escape it only because their inputs also carry `required` themselves. Rajeev's ruling says required fields carry `required` **on the element**.
- **fix, recommended by T-166 and the work manager:** make `Field` pass `required` into the props it hands its child, so the input carries it wherever `Field` says *"(required)"*. One change fixes every `Field`; a page-by-page fix would leave the same trap for the next screen. **Sweep first:** list every `Field` with `required`, whether its input already carries `required`, and which tests submit a blank box there, because those tests change meaning.
- **expected knock-on:** `tenant-new.test.tsx` submits with blank coordinates, admin name and email, so it will need those filled in; sign-in, tenant edit, Settings and any other `Field` screen are checked the same way.
- **paths (checked at dispatch):** `frontend/components/Field.tsx`, and the tests of every screen whose `Field` gains `required` (at least `tenant-new`, `tenant-edit`, `signin`, `sign-out`, `settings-payments`, `settings-warnings`, `meal-kinds`, `occasions`, `meal-composer`), plus a new `Field` test.
- **wave:** **after slices E and F (T-165, T-166) are proven**, since T-165's `meal-composer` tests render `Field`; and **before T-169b**, which rewrites the Settings screen that uses `Field`.
- **approved:** the main session, 2026-09-13, option 1 (`Field` passes `required` through), sequenced after slices E and F and before T-169b; easy to reverse. **Two conditions:**
  1. **A blank coordinate on Add a temple must never become 0.** That is T-041's defect, a temple silently relocated to 0,0. The proof shows a blank or cleared coordinate is refused, or stays null, **on both the client and the server**. ### T-175 — A `Form`'s sentence placed outside its own form element may not survive a re-render — queued, not dispatched

- **source:** found by T-165, 2026-09-13; queued by the work manager. **Unproven:** no test showed a failure.
- **what:** on `/volunteers/[id]`, the Take a volunteer off form is empty and reached by `form=`; its boxes live in the attendance form's table. So `Form` puts the removal form's sentences inside **another** form's DOM. T-160's `MutationObserver` watches only its own form element, so if that table re-renders while a sentence shows, the sentence may not be put back or may be lost.
- **do:** first write a test that re-renders the attendance table while a removal sentence is showing, and see whether it fails. Fix `Form.tsx` only if it does, e.g. by also watching each refused control's own parent. If it passes, record that and close.

- **wave:** after wave 3-2's merged check. It must not run beside T-174 if T-174 touches `form-wrapper.test.tsx`; the work manager checks at dispatch.
- **state:** **proven** 2026-09-13 (`docs/work/proof/T-175.md`). **The suspected defect is not real, and `Form.tsx` is unchanged.** Every re-render a person can cause on the roster keeps each removal sentence right after its box's label, once, with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` intact. React inserts new nodes before nodes it rendered itself, so it never puts anything between a box and the slot `Form` placed after it; the observer watching only the empty removal form costs nothing on this page. **Two tests added to `shift-attendance.test.tsx`:** the table stays up through unticking a volunteer, opening *"Send update to all"* and a held-open attendance save, and the sentences then clear as the boxes are filled; and a data refresh takes the whole roster down (*"Loading roster…"*), leaves nothing behind, and the next press shows each sentence once. **Controls, each restored by `cmp`:** (1) `Form` never places a slot: 4 red, at first display; (2) slot placed once, never put back, observer inert: all 60 green, which is what shows neither mechanism is needed here; (3) the feared fault injected, a slot dropped on re-render: the new test red right after *"Send update to all"* opens. `tsc` clean; `shift-attendance`, `form-wrapper` and four run-only files 122/122; ESLint clean. Full vitest 1,773/1,775, both failures in `phone.test.ts`, T-186's file in flight. **Follow-ups, not queued:** (a) **T-160's re-render test in `form-wrapper.test.tsx` stayed green under control 2**, so it does not prove what T-160's proof says (that `Form` puts a disturbed sentence back); only reordering a keyed list of boxes would exercise it. (b) **The roster page's reload after every save takes the whole roster down**, so anything typed into an open removal form is lost, not only the sentence; fixing it means the page or its data hook. ### T-159 — Six WhatsApp templates refused by Meta, the test message filed as Marketing, and a templates date that never gets written

- **source:** staging, 2026-09-12, reported by the main session. Rajeev connected South Bengaluru's WhatsApp (Meta's test number; phone number id 1211371598734181, WABA 2154813661742453). The API logged *"Submitted 14 of 20 WhatsApp templates"*. Meta refused six, with these messages from `MetaWhatsAppClient`:
  - `shift_reminder`, `po_delivery`, `shift_broadcast`, `temple_announcement`: *"This template has too many variables for its length. Reduce the number of variables or increase the message length."*
  - `temple_communication`: *"The message body can't have more than two consecutive newline characters, only have parameters, or have more than 10 emojis."*
  - `low_stock_digest`: *"Variables can't be at the start or end of the template."*
  - `connection_test` (T-151) was accepted but shows **In review, with Meta's category set to Marketing**, although we submit it as UTILITY. Meta does not deliver marketing templates to US numbers, and Rajeev's test phone is a US number.
- **Staging evidence for the null date** (main session, read through the API, not the database): the `PUT /api/v1/settings/whatsapp` started 00:10:51Z, took 64.75s and returned 200. *"Submitted 14 of 20 …"* was logged at 00:11:56.393Z with the same request id. A signed-in GET at 00:13:12Z returned `templatesSubmittedAt: null`, while `phoneNumberId`, `wabaId` and `displayNumber` from the same save were updated. There was no WARN or ERROR in that window apart from the six refusals. The code sets `whatsapp_templates_submitted_at` whenever at least one template was submitted, so the UPDATE matched nothing or never ran. Cause not yet proven.
- **wave:** 3a — alone.
- **state:** **proven** 2026-09-13, backend parts only; the screen parts are still held. **The null date's cause, proven: the write landed and the read threw it away.** `read()` used `queryForMap`, and the PostgreSQL driver returns `timestamptz` as `java.sql.Timestamp`. The old `instant()` accepted only `OffsetDateTime` and returned null for anything else. So **`verifiedAt`, `webhookSeenAt` and `templatesSubmittedAt` have read null for every temple since the feature was written** (`ccc9635`, 2026-08-16). The transaction, `app.tenant_id`, the pool and `tenancy/` were not involved; the main session's two guesses were both wrong, and the brief had said so. Evidence: `WhatsAppTemplateSubmissionIT` runs the service in a real transaction, reads the column straight from `tenant_settings` as the app role (set), then GETs the view (null), which is staging's symptom. A pinning test shows the driver type. Control B was red on the untouched code, at the GET, after the table assertion passed. Control B2 put the old read back into the fixed code and went red again. Fix: a row mapper reading each date with `getObject(column, OffsetDateTime.class)`. **Staging check the main session can make without the database:** the same GET that returned `templatesSubmittedAt: null` should also show `verifiedAt: null`, and Settings should never have shown "Last checked" for WhatsApp. The date is stamped when at least one template was accepted or already existed (unchanged rule). The `whatsapp_verified_at` write was fine and its read had the same defect; `whatsapp_last_sent_at` is read as a boolean and was never affected. **Part 1:** kept one sentence per message, so the six rewordings change the SMS and email text too; none was ever approved at Meta. `MetaTemplateRulesTest` checks every template for: no body that is only parameters, no more than two newlines in a row, no more than 10 emoji (source: Meta's staging refusal); no parameter at the start or end (source: Meta's template-review page); and at least 3 fixed words per parameter. **Meta publishes no length threshold.** Two providers publish words + parameters ≥ 3n + 1, which matches all 20 staging outcomes, and the test is slightly stricter. Control A (the old shift reminder restored): 2 red, both naming `shift_reminder`. **Part 2:** the test template is renamed **`whatsapp_connection_check`**, UTILITY, reworded as a plain statement of what was checked and who asked. Meta's docs: a template in review cannot be edited, an approved template's category cannot be changed, and a deleted name cannot be reused for 30 days; so a new name was required. The old `connection_test` stays in the Meta account, unused. Meta's edit endpoint needs a template id we never store, so it is not a one-call fix. **Part 4:** `V128` adds `tenant_settings.whatsapp_refused_templates JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` (DDL only; RLS already on the table), replaced on every save, holding each refused template's name and a plain reason. A template Meta could not be reached for is stored too. Returned as `TenantWhatsAppSettings.refusedTemplates`; `api.ts` untouched. Control C (the store removed): 3 of 7 red. Builder's final run: 10 contract classes plus `ErrorCodeTest`, **827/827**. **Merged backend check, work manager, no builder in the tree:** run 1, the same eleven classes, `--rerun-tasks`, **827/827**; run 2, the six tests outside the contract that use the templates or WhatsApp settings (`NotificationIT` 7, `NotificationSendE2EIT` 1, `PurchaseOrderWhatsAppIT` 8, `DonationIntakeIT` 13, `WishlistContributionIT` 9, `ShiftAttendanceIT` 28), **66/66**. No frontend file changed, so no frontend run. Log: `scratchpad/merged-backend-T159.log`. **T-159 is proven and not released.** Files: the four `notification/` main files, `V128__whatsapp_refused_templates.sql`, `NotificationTemplateTest.java`, `WhatsAppTestSendIT.java`, `MetaTemplateRulesTest.java` *(new)*, `WhatsAppTemplateSubmissionIT.java` *(new)*, `docs/work/proof/T-159.md`. UAT-022 and UAT-066 needed no change. **Follow-ups, not queued:** show `refusedTemplates` on Settings (held with the redesign); `ErrorCode.java:1046`'s comment and `docs/META_WHATSAPP_SETUP.md` still name `connection_test`; a multi-line shift broadcast will be refused on WhatsApp because Meta allows no newline inside a parameter (predates this task); `DonationVoidService:176` has a similar `OffsetDateTime`-only check worth a look. **Needed on staging after release:** press Save on Settings → WhatsApp so the six rewordings and the new test template reach Meta, with Rajeev's approval.
- **what, dispatched now (backend):**
  1. Rewrite the six refused templates so they meet Meta's three rules, keeping what each says, and add a test that enforces the rules on every `NotificationTemplate`.
  2. Make the connection test unmistakably a utility message. Establish from Meta's documentation whether an existing template can be re-categorised or edited, or whether it needs a new name, and what happens to the old one.
  3. Prove why `whatsapp_templates_submitted_at` stays null after a partial submission, and fix it. Check the `whatsapp_verified_at` and `whatsapp_last_sent_at` writes for the same shape.
  4. Store which templates Meta refused, and why, and return them on the settings view (`V128`).
- **HELD, not dispatched — waiting on Rajeev's ruling on a Settings redesign (see below):** showing the refused templates on the Settings screen, and saying which box is missing when Save is greyed out (`frontend/app/settings/page.tsx` ~:977, per the required-fields ruling: *"App secret is required"* in red).

The six refused ones were never created, so they go in on the next Save. Any future wording change to an existing template goes nowhere today, unless T-159 finds that Meta's edit call makes it a one-call fix, in which case it reports back first.

### T-156 — `ds/Button` defaults to `type="button"`, and every in-form caller says `type="submit"`

- **source:** the main session, 2026-09-12, from the defect that removed an order line and saved the
  order with the line still on it: a `Button` inside a `<form>` with no `type` is a submit button.
- **wave:** 2b — alone, after T-154 and T-157 land.
- **state:** **proven** 2026-09-12. `Button` now defaults `type = "button"` in its props, written after `{...rest}` so a forwarded `type={undefined}` cannot bring the submit back. **The sweep changed no caller:** parsing every `.tsx` with the TypeScript compiler found 181 `Button`s; every one inside a form, or pointing at one with `form=`, already said `type="submit"` or `type="button"`, and the 85 untyped ones are all outside forms (parent/child placements traced both ways). All 21 forms with no internal submit still submit (18 by a header `form=` button, one by its own `form=` button, one by a row button, and the communications composer never submits on purpose). Raw `<button>`s in forms with no type: 0. Control A (default removed): 4 of 6 new tests red; the 2 green pass either way. Control B (no typed caller existed, so run on the two Settings Add forms whose only submit is an explicit `type="submit"`): 5 existing tests red. All restores by `cmp`. Builder's final run over the tree with T-154 and T-157 in it: `tsc` clean, vitest 127 files / 1,518, ESLint clean. **Deviations, both accepted:** `@testing-library/user-event` is not installed and `package.json` was outside the contract, so the test uses `fireEvent.click` (jsdom's own button activation decides submission); jsdom cannot press Enter, so the test asserts the form's default button is save, not an earlier remove. **Follow-up, not queued:** adding `user-event` so tests can press Tab and Enter — a dependency decision.
- **what:** `frontend/components/ds/Button.tsx` spreads `...rest` onto a `<button>` with no `type`, so
  every `Button` inside a form submits it. Default `type` to `"button"` (a caller's explicit `type`
  still wins). Then sweep every caller that sits inside a `<form>` — in the same file, or rendered by a
  component that a parent places inside a form — and that relied on the implicit submit, so each says
  `type="submit"` explicitly. For each file the proof lists which buttons became `type="submit"` and
  why each is the form's submit. Raw `<button>` elements are out of scope; count those in forms with no
  `type` and report the number, but do not change them. **Negative control:** a new test renders a
  `Button` inside a `<form>` and asserts pressing it does not submit; remove the default and show that
  test go red. Anchor, `cp` snapshot, `cmp -s`, `trap … EXIT`, artefacts named `control-T-156.*`.
- **paths:** `frontend/components/ds/Button.tsx` · every file under `frontend/app/` and
  `frontend/components/` that imports `ds/Button` (re-checked at dispatch after T-157: 68 files import `ds/Button"`, plus `components/ds/ButtonLink.tsx` via `./Button`; list at `scratchpad/button-importers-T-156.txt`) · every test
  under `frontend/__tests__/` (granted as a glob because the task runs alone) ·
  `frontend/__tests__/button-type.test.tsx` *(new)*.

### T-157 — A phone number typed with spaces is refused, including the example in the error itself

- **source:** found by T-151, 2026-09-12 · the main session's line-up for wave 2.
- **wave:** 2a
- **state:** **proven** 2026-09-12. Backend 166/166 across eight classes (`PhoneNormalisationIT` 84, through the app's own `ObjectMapper` and `Validator`: nine fields times seven ways of typing, plus typo, `(0)` and blank boundaries). Frontend `tsc` and ESLint clean, 9 files 123/123. **Mechanism:** `config/PhoneNumberDeserializer`, put with `@JsonDeserialize` beside each `@Pattern`, so validation sees the stripped value; the regexp and `GlobalExceptionHandler` are unchanged. It strips whitespace (including non-breaking), dashes (`\p{Pd}`) and invisible format characters; **not brackets** (a `(0)` trunk digit kept would store a number that rings nobody) and not dots. Frontend `lib/phone.ts` (`normalizePhone`, `isE164`) is used by register, sign-in, choose-temple, settings test box, staff hire and edit, vendor add and edit, and tenants/new; Firebase gets the bare number. Server control (stripping removed): 71 red, restore by `cmp`. Frontend control (trim only): 19 red, restore by `cmp`. **Nine fields, not eight** as this row first said. **Behaviour change to tell Rajeev:** Add a temple used to strip everything but digits, so `+91 98765 4321X` or `+91 (0) 80…` became a well-formed wrong number; both are now refused with `KMS-400003`. **Follow-ups, not queued:** `GlobalExceptionHandler`'s comment still says eight fields; the Java and JS separator lists are kept in step by hand only. Out of scope and unchanged: kitchen, event contact, equipment service company and donor phones (no E.164 rule). No hand test.
- **what:** `KMS-400003` says *"Include the country code, for example +91 98765 43210"*, and that
  number is refused. The server's rule is `@Pattern("^\+[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$")` on nine fields (corrected from eight by T-157):
  `HireStaffRequest` (phone, emergencyContactPhone), `UpdateStaffRequest` (same two),
  `JoinTempleRequest`, `ProvisionTenantRequest.adminPhone`, `Create/UpdateVendorRequest`,
  `SendWhatsAppTestRequest`. The frontend trims but keeps inner spaces, and repeats the regex in
  `register/page.tsx:83` and `JoinTempleForm.tsx:48`; only `tenants/new/page.tsx` strips
  (`normalizePhone`). Accept spaces and hyphens (and the invisible characters `normalizePhone` already
  handles) by stripping them before validation on both sides, so what is stored is canonical E.164.
  The regexp itself stays exactly as it is, because `GlobalExceptionHandler` recognises a phone error by
  that string. Firebase phone sign-in must receive the stripped number too. Fields with no `@Pattern`
  (a kitchen's contact number, a donor's phone) are out of scope. The proof names every input this
  reaches, server and screen.
- **paths:** backend — the seven request records above under `backend/src/main/java/org/iskcon/kms/`
  (`staff/HireStaffRequest.java`, `staff/UpdateStaffRequest.java`, `tenant/JoinTempleRequest.java`,
  `tenant/ProvisionTenantRequest.java`, `vendor/CreateVendorRequest.java`,
  `vendor/UpdateVendorRequest.java`, `notification/SendWhatsAppTestRequest.java`),
  `config/PhoneNumberDeserializer.java` *(new, only if a shared deserializer is the chosen mechanism)*;
  tests `error/PhoneValidationIT.java`, `tenant/TenantProvisioningIT.java`, `tenant/MembershipIT.java`,
  `notification/WhatsAppTestSendIT.java`, `staff/StaffEmploymentIT.java`, `vendor/VendorIT.java`,
  `vendor/VendorWithoutPhoneIT.java` (existing, granted), `error/PhoneNormalisationIT.java` *(new)*.
  Frontend — `frontend/lib/phone.ts` *(new)*, `app/register/page.tsx`, `app/sign-in/page.tsx`,
  `components/JoinTempleForm.tsx`, `app/settings/page.tsx` (the test-number box only),
  `components/staff/StaffForm.tsx`, `app/vendors/new/page.tsx`, `app/vendors/[id]/page.tsx`,
  `app/tenants/new/page.tsx`; tests `register.test.tsx`, `signin.test.tsx`, `choose-temple.test.tsx`,
  `settings-payments.test.tsx`, `staff-hire.test.tsx`, `vendors.test.tsx`,

### T-152 — `NotificationSendE2EIT` flakes, and the timeout is not the fix

- **source:** `WORK_QUEUE.md` / `THE-REST.md` §3 · Wave A's CI red (run 34570919636) · `fc03d6a` papered over the first symptom.
- **wave:** 1b — after T-151, because the likely mechanism lives in the same package.
- **state:** **proven** 2026-09-12. **The mechanism, which the ledger had wrong:** the test's comment said it shared a context with `BackgroundJobIT`, but its `@MockBean` and extra property give it its own. So two schedulers named `kms-scheduler` polled one clustered Quartz store. `notify()` writes the job inside the caller's transaction, and Quartz nudges its thread before commit, so the thread finds nothing and sleeps 24-30s. Whichever node woke first sent the message: its own scheduler, 24-30s late (the old timeout); or the other context's, which has no mail sender or from address, so every channel failed (the CI `FAILED`). **Far-side evidence:** CI run 34570919636's report shows the send 20s after queueing with "from address unset", an address the E2E context does set. A local reproduction held the transaction open and watched the other node take the job and fail. **Fix, test configuration only:** a scheduler name of its own (`kms-scheduler-notification-e2e`) and a 1s idle wait. The test now holds its transaction open for a second on every run, so the race is always exercised. The await dropped from 30s to 10s, and a failure message now lists each attempt. `NotificationService` was deliberately untouched: the API runs no scheduler in production, and scheduling after commit would give up atomicity. **5 consecutive runs** of both classes with `--rerun-tasks`: 6/6 each time. Control, both settings removed and idle wait alone removed: `PENDING`, 1 of 1 each; restore proved by `cmp`. The wrong-node half has no deterministic control; it rests on the CI log and the reproduction, and the proof says so. Comments corrected in `WhatsAppChannelAdapter`, `PurchaseOrderDetailView` and `BackgroundJobIT`. **Follow-up, not queued:** `RecipeDocumentE2EIT` may carry the same late-pickup shape; unchecked.
- **what:** It has failed two ways: timed out still pending, and terminally `FAILED` where `SENT` was
  expected. Its recipient prefers WhatsApp, and its temple has no WhatsApp settings, so the adapter
  fails and the message must cascade to email (a mocked `JavaMailSender`). It shares a
  scheduler-enabled context with `jobs/BackgroundJobIT`. Find the mechanism, with evidence from the
  far side (the `notification_attempts` rows for a failing run), and fix that. Raising the timeout
  again is not a fix.
- **paths:** `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/notification/NotificationSendE2EIT.java`,
  `backend/src/test/java/org/iskcon/kms/jobs/BackgroundJobIT.java`; main code in
  `backend/src/main/java/org/iskcon/kms/notification/` **only** where the mechanism is proved to be,
  each file named in the proof. The work manager checked that no other 1b contract is in that package.
- **reservations:** none.
- **proof:** `docs/work/proof/T-152.md`

The per-wave blocks further down are historical and several of their summaries are stale — this
block is the one that is maintained.

> **The block that used to be here was written on 2026-09-08 and was read as current for eleven

> more than a day after 2026-09-10, check it against `git log` before you trust a number in it.**

### Where the work stands

`kms-staging-worker-00128-l9m`, all on image tag `20260910-200950`, schema `V122`.** Waves 15 to 21
all shipped on 2026-09-10.

**Wave 21's live check, and what it proves — read this before concluding the shopping list is
broken.** `GET /api/v1/shopping-list` answers **200 with an empty array**, and that is correct rather
than a failure. The only two ingredients in the tenant that are below their reorder level — Amla and

PO-2026-0029 SENT and -0039, -0042 DRAFT), and D-24a says an ingredient a live order already covers
leaves the list. Six of the twelve live orders were raised from the shopping list on 2026-09-10, so

Three numbers are deliberate gaps and none is a missing file: `V105`, `V108` and `V109` were

## ✅ WAVE A — SHIPPED AND VERIFIED ON STAGING, 2026-09-11

**Staging is now `kms-staging-api-00147-q8k` / `kms-staging-web-00135-jmv` /
`kms-staging-worker-00129-2zh`, schema `V123`. The next free migration number is `V124`.**

Four commits, one per task: `0622762` (T-105), `ef63831` (T-116), `190ea29` (T-076),
`68d4cf4` (T-135 + T-136). CI run **34570919636** green on all three jobs. `V123` confirmed applied
from the API's own startup log, not from the deploy's exit code.

**All four were driven in a browser as the role they were written for**, signed in as the Temple
Admin and — for the refusal — as an identity the server refuses. What that found is below.

### The two things the recon changed before a line was written, both from reading the tree rather than the ledger

- **T-105's row was stale.** It described the mistyped-enum case answering `KMS-500001` with an HTTP
  500. Commit `bed58c8` had already made it a 400. What was actually left was the third and sharpest
  of its three complaints: the answer **named no field and no allowed values**, so it said *"Check
  the highlighted fields"* with nothing highlighted.
- **`POST /settings/whatsapp/test` does not send a message.** It calls `meta.verifyNumber(...)`, a
  credential check, and stamps `whatsapp_verified_at`. So every field on `TenantWhatsAppSettings`
  says *configured*, and gating T-136 on any of them would have defeated Rajeev's ruling exactly as
  that row warned. **T-136 therefore added a new fact** — `tenant_settings.whatsapp_last_sent_at`
  (`V123`), stamped in one place only, after Meta returns a message id.

### What each task turned out to be

- **T-105** — split by where the bad value came from. A `@PathVariable` that cannot convert stays a
  **404** (*a path that identifies nothing is a 404*); a `@RequestParam` becomes a **400 naming the
  field**, because `/orders?status=SNET` names a real collection and one misspelt word, and *"We
  couldn't find what you were looking for"* sent the reader hunting for an order that exists. Field
  and allowed values are read from `MismatchedInputException.getPath()` and
  `getTargetType().getEnumConstants()` — never from Jackson's message string, so its wording cannot
  leak. No new error code; `400148` was allocated and **not taken, so it returns to the pool.**
- **T-116** — `REFUSALS` holds **two** codes and both were mute, in different ways. `KMS-400020`'s
  words had never been on a screen. `KMS-400019`'s **were** on screen — as two string literals
  retyped by hand into the JSX, which is a coincidence rather than a mechanism. **The proof that it
  was a coincidence is one constant away:** T-114 reworded `KMS-400020` the day before and nothing in
  the app moved. A new guard test asserts the words *arrive*, where `ErrorCodeTest` only ever
  asserted they exist — and a fifth assertion forbids a catalogue message from becoming a heading's
  accessible name, so nobody is ever pressed to trim a full stop off stored copy.
- **T-076** — ESLint 10 flat config, `eslint-plugin-testing-library`, **12 rules, zero style rules**,
  wired into the CI frontend job. The `"lint"` script had to change to `eslint . --max-warnings=0`:
  Next 14's wrapper wants an `.eslintrc` and cannot read flat config, so leaving it would have given
  **a linter that exits 0 having checked nothing.** Two real findings fixed.
- **T-135 + T-136** — built as one task because they are one file and one question.

### `KMS-400020` was reworded, and the reason is the general one

*"You're signed in, but you don't have an account at **this** temple yet"* → *"…at **any** temple
yet."* `AuthenticationFilter:147` raises it in the branch where `found.isEmpty()` and `TenantContext`
has just been **cleared** — the reader is a member of nowhere, and there is no "this temple" anywhere
in the request that reaches it. Established from the far side rather than from the constant's own
wording. The next step is deliberately **not** rendered and is now exempt by name in the guard, with
the reasoning in a comment on the constant: it would repeat the heading of the screen it lands on.

### The best find of the wave, and no test could have caught it

**The Remove button on an order line carried no `type`.** Inside a `<form>` that defaults to
`type="submit"`, so pressing Remove removed the line **and submitted the order** — and `saveLines`
read the pre-update `draftLines`, so it **saved the order with the removed line still on it.** The
row vanished on re-render, so it looked like it had worked until the next load brought the line back.

**The existing test was green because it only asserted the button was *disabled* on a one-line
draft** — the single case where pressing it does nothing.

**The generalisation, and it is now a thing to grep for:** `frontend/components/ds/Button.tsx`
spreads `...rest` onto a bare `<button>` and **does not default the `type`**, so every caller that
omits it inherits HTML's submit default. One line there closes it application-wide. **That file was
outside the contract and is queued, not done.**

### What the browser found that the suite did not — one defect, open

**On `/orders/<id>` in edit mode the order's lines render twice:** the editable table, and the
read-only view table still rendered underneath it, between Save/Cancel and the cancel block.
Confirmed in the DOM on `web-00135-jmv`, not by eye. **Routed to T-134's builder**, which already
holds that file — and it matters there more than here, because T-134 mounts that same editor as a
panel over the shopping list, where a stray read-only copy would be worse.

Everything else on that screen verified clean and does **not** need re-checking: button order, the
two labels, no *"Stop editing"*, the cancel block at the foot of both modes, Remove enabled at full
opacity, `whatsappMentioned: false`, and **zero typeless buttons inside a form remaining** on the
deployed build.

### Browser verification is no longer blocked on Rajeev, and the note that said it was is wrong

The session memory recorded the IndexedDB write needed to put a minted token into the browser as
**refused by the auto-mode classifier, therefore needing Rajeev once**. **It went through with no
prompt on 2026-09-11** and all of Wave A was verified with it. Mint an ID token with a Firebase
custom token signed by the admin SDK service account, `put` the auth record into
`firebaseLocalStorageDb` → `firebaseLocalStorage`, navigate. **No password is typed at any point** —
typing one into the sign-in form stays prohibited and is never necessary. Swapping the record for a
different account is how a *refused* identity gets driven, which is the only way to see an auth
refusal on a real screen, and it is how T-116 was proved.

### One CI red that was not the code, and not the known OOM either

`NotificationSendE2EIT > notify() queues a message that the background worker then sends` failed with
`expected: "SENT" but was: "FAILED"`. **One assertion, zero others, 2222 tests completed.** The
tree-comparison check the ledger prescribes could not be used — commit 4 genuinely changes
`backend/` — so the release agent established it from the code path instead: that test's temple has
no WhatsApp settings, so the adapter returns `failed(...)` before reaching any line this wave
touched, and the new stamp sits on the far side of that early return. Re-run on the identical tree:
green. **It has been papered over once before** (`fc03d6a`, which raised its timeout) and this is a
*different* symptom of the same test — last time it timed out still pending, this time the send
terminally failed. **It is a real flake with a real mechanism and it wants its own row.**

### Open, and carried forward rather than guessed

1. **An expired session falls through to the temple picker**, so a year-long volunteer is asked which
   temple they serve at, roughly hourly. `KMS-400018 SESSION_EXPIRED` exists and **nothing raises
   it**; the silence is deliberate, because expired and forged tokens are refused by the same path
   and explaining expiry hands an attacker a bit they do not have. **Security posture — Rajeev's.**
   Written up in decision shape with three options in `docs/work/proof/T-116.md`.
2. **The WhatsApp chicken-and-egg.** The button appears only after a send, so a temple using WhatsApp
   *only* for purchase orders never earns it. Other channels stamp the same column, so it largely
   self-closes. **The clean fix is making the settings Test button send a real message** — which is
   what Rajeev was told already existed when he asked whether a test-send could be the trigger.
   **Queued as a task, not a question.**
3. **`ds/Button.tsx` does not default `type`** — see above.
4. **`react-hooks` rules are referenced and undefined.** `app/planner/reuse/page.tsx:156` and
   `components/planner/MealComposer.tsx:376` carry `eslint-disable-next-line
   react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` for a rule nothing in the repo defines. Adding
   `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` with `rules-of-hooks` is worth doing and is its own task; T-076
   correctly did not widen into it.
